title: Oral Care During Pregnancy: A Guide for Expectant Mothers
excerpt: Proper oral care during pregnancy ensures health for mom and baby.
content:
## Summary
Oral care during pregnancy is crucial for maintaining the health of both the mother and the fetus. Hormonal changes during pregnancy can affect the gums and teeth, making them more susceptible to problems. Proper oral care can help prevent complications and ensure a healthy pregnancy. This article will provide guidance on how to care for your teeth and gums during pregnancy, including dietary adjustments, proper brushing techniques, and safe products to use.

## Practical tips
To maintain good oral health during pregnancy, follow these practical tips:
- Eat a balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins to provide essential nutrients for your teeth and gums.
- Brush your teeth at least twice a day with a fluoride toothpaste and soft-bristled toothbrush, paying special attention to the gum line.
- Floss once a day to remove food particles and plaque from between your teeth.
- Use a mouthwash that is safe for pregnant women to help kill bacteria and freshen your breath.
- Visit your dentist regularly for check-ups and cleanings to prevent and detect any oral health problems early.
- Avoid sugary and acidic foods and drinks that can contribute to tooth decay and erosion.
- If you experience any oral health issues, such as bleeding gums or tooth pain, contact your dentist promptly for advice.

## When to seek care
If you experience any of the following symptoms, seek dental care promptly:
- Severe toothache or gum pain
- Bleeding or swelling of the gums
- Loose teeth or changes in your bite
- Pain or difficulty when eating or drinking
- White patches or sores in your mouth
- Fever or swollen lymph nodes

## FAQs:
Q1: Is it safe to go to the dentist during pregnancy?
A1: Yes, it is safe to go to the dentist during pregnancy. In fact, regular dental check-ups are important for maintaining good oral health and preventing complications.
Q2: Can I use mouthwash during pregnancy?
A2: Yes, you can use mouthwash during pregnancy, but choose a product that is safe for pregnant women and follow the instructions carefully.
Q3: How can I prevent morning sickness from affecting my teeth?
A3: To prevent morning sickness from affecting your teeth, rinse your mouth with water or a fluoride mouthwash after vomiting, and avoid brushing your teeth immediately after vomiting as the acid can damage your tooth enamel. Instead, wait at least 30 minutes before brushing your teeth.
